notes: MCP TOOLS. Read rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs and utils.rs first: implement `Tool` for each tool (`def()` returns `ToolDef::new("<name>", "<description>", <schema>)` with the name as a string literal at that call, the description copied verbatim from the TypeScript because it is prompt text, and the schema being the zod schema converted to JSON Schema: same property names, types, enums, defaults, limits, descriptions and required list), and expose `pub fn register(registry: &mut ToolRegistry)` from lib.rs. Output text must equal the TypeScript's: same wording, same JSON shape and key order (serde_json's preserve_order feature is enabled in this crate, keep it). The scope, fence, findings scope, findings dedupe and tenant logic is already ported in rever-scope: use it as a path dependency and keep its checks exactly where the TypeScript has them, since they are the safety boundary of Red Team scans. findings.ts stores findings and exports reports, using Electron for the data folder, save dialogs and the renderer bridge: store under `ctx.data_dir` with the same file names and JSON shapes, write exports to the path the arguments give or to the same default location under the data folder, and where the TypeScript notifies the interface (renderer bridge), emit through a callback or channel held in `ctx.state::<T>()` that the app can subscribe to later (default: nothing listens). scan.ts starts scans through the interface: the same approach. Page access is only through `ctx.browser`; when nothing matches, do NOT edit rever-tools-api: return `utils::err(tool::unsupported("<what>"))` and list it under behaviorDifferences. Async: `call` returns a boxed future run on a tokio runtime; tests use #[tokio::test] and a temporary directory as data_dir. A tool file gets the `Port of` marker when all of its tools are registered.
